field-values: Pick two different places at the same time. How many readings could you ask the field to give you?
Imagine drawing a different number at each spot on a map. Would it still be a map?
field-mode: Freeze the clock. Which part of the expression could you still change by moving to another place?
Find the input in q(t). Where would you put a position on the right side?
mode-energy: Write the energy for two neighboring counts and subtract. What happens to the half in both expressions?
Try the gaps between three successive counts. What in the formula would make one gap bigger than another?
above-vacuum: Turn the count of excitations down to zero. Which rule still describes the field?
Compare the lowest level with a level below it. Does this model offer a lower step to release energy into?
natural-units: Try measuring time in the distance light travels. Would changing the ruler and clock units stop light from moving?
Think about what the number one is replacing here. Is that choice about the available units or the material surrounding the light?
field-action: Metres and seconds name units. Could knowing a unit tell you whether a graph bends up or down?
Picture a hilltop and a valley bottom. How steep is the slope at the very centre of each?
scalar-lagrangian: Check the signs of the spatial and mass terms before using the expression as stored energy.
Distance and height can share a unit while measuring different things. What role does ℒ play in this calculation?
field-motion: A motion rule can admit several possible preparations. What information would select one of them?
Changing the mass changes one term in the motion rule. Where is the preparation of the field specified?
field-momentum: Read the definition of π on the left before setting a spatial change to zero. Which rate is used here?
Could the number in this equation change as the field changes? Compare that with the number for the circumference of a circle.
free-dispersion: Insert a chosen wave number and mass on the right. What freedom is left on the other side?
What condition must the wave pattern satisfy before you interpret one of its excitations as a particle?
canonical-commutator: Find the two mode labels on the small delta symbol. What does it check about those labels?
Imagine two different patterns that repeat equally fast. Would that give them the same mode label?
mode-field-operator: An average can be zero even when readings vary. What would you need to predict that spread?
Follow what Q does when applied to a state. How does that compare with looking up an ordinary number on a map?
vacuum-mode-variance: The example includes one wave pattern. How many patterns can contribute to a field reading at a place?
Check what Q names in the calculation. Would reusing a letter guarantee that two measurements are identical?
create-quantum: Try a starting count for which the square-root factor exceeds one. What range is possible for a probability?
Change n on both sides and ask what the factor multiplies. Does its role change at the first occupied level?
remove-quantum: Compare the zero result from applying the removal rule to an empty mode with energy leaving a real system.
Follow the other parts of the interacting system. Where else could the energy of an absorbed excitation appear?
fock-normalization: Apply the creation rule twice and keep both square-root factors. What size does the resulting state have?
A starting state can have length one. Does every operation you apply keep that length?
mode-momentum: Reverse the direction of a moving particle. Which quantity needs a sign to show that direction?
Put opposite momentum directions into the massless energy rule. Does the energy use the signed component or its size?
quartic-interaction: In the interaction term, which factor sets its strength even before a particular wave pattern is picked?
Look up the role of λ in this particular equation. What does doubling it do to the interaction term?
tree-amplitude: Which quantity can have a minus sign before you take its size squared?
Change the sign of λ and compare the size squared before and after. What does the sign alone tell you?
scalar-propagator: Add the incoming and outgoing energies at one meeting point. Which rule does that comparison test?
The internal line is part of a calculation. Where are energy and momentum matched between connected pieces?
amplitude-interference: Try two real contributions of the same size with opposite signs. Does the order of adding and squaring matter?
Compare squaring a sum with summing two squares. Which calculation keeps the effect of the contributions reinforcing each other?
cross-section-scaling: Suppose you know a quantity doubled. What else would you need to give its new value in square metres?
A ratio can be a pure number. Where would the units of an absolute scattering area come from?
momentum-cutoff: Repeat the calculation with a different upper bound. What would show whether a physical prediction depends on that choice?
Look at the upper bound inside the logarithm. Does simply choosing a large value test independence?
match-a-parameter: Compare reproducing a point used to set the parameter with predicting a different measurement. Which is an independent check?
Could two different curves pass through the same measured point?
running-coupling: Keep the experimental setup fixed and change the reference scale used in the calculation. What else must be recalculated?
If one part varies with scale, what do the other parts of the full prediction do?
effective-theory: Look for the word “illustrative” beside the formula. Which assumption set the power in this particular estimate?
A small energy ratio makes higher powers smaller. Does that tell you which power the physical rules allow first?
perturbation-check: Compare the sign of one term with the size of many later terms. Which controls what happens far down the series?
Could a later term grow even if the first correction was small? What additional pattern would you need to check?
